target_name: Dual Profit Measure With Term Funding
rationale: This is essentially the average of two already-tested signals that share the identical NEG(dlc/lt) quality leg, so the expected gain is a rank-averaging smoothing artifact rather than new economic content, and the "complementary measurement error" story is asserted rather than tested.

The worst-case TS_MAX operator is a legitimate and sign-consistent reframing of the archive's best quality leg, but because dlc/lt is highly persistent the five-year maximum will be strongly collinear with the already-tested level, limiting incremental information.

Coherent and correctly signed consolidation of the two strongest archive quality legs, though the claim of near-orthogonality is overstated since both legs are built from current assets and current liabilities, and one leg is a coarse 0–5 count that will contribute mostly ties.

EBITDA-to-total-debt is a standard credit metric that is close to a rediscovery of the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite, and because both legs share oibdp in the numerator the "interaction" largely double-counts profitability rather than isolating debt capacity, with low- and zero-debt firms driving the extreme ranks even after winsorising.

The re-scaling of EBITDA volatility to assets is a genuine diagnosis-driven fix of the archive's size-contaminated volatility leg, and the additive SUMRANK correctly implements the stated substitutability of stability and funding safety, though the result will sit close to conventional quality/low-earnings-volatility exposure.

The industry-neutralisation is a defensible targeted response to the margin signal's high-alpha/low-slope/low-Sharpe pathology, but simultaneously swapping the liquidity leg from dlc/lt to dlc/act makes it a three-way recombination of existing archive entries whose attribution will be ambiguous, and the archive already showed IND_RANK did not improve the asset-scaled version.
